principles: RED must be visible: every wired guard is an invariant that must never sit RED unnoticed; the gate exists to surface failures, never to be relaxed to pass.
Minimal blast radius: touch only package.json scripts (+ optionally an aggregator); never alter guard/smoke assertion logic or gitRoot/process-fact-registry code.
No double-running: a guard already in the chain (gitroot-cwd-contract) must not be added again.
Fast gate stays fast: per-commit/REVIEW->TEST path runs only fast invariants; genuinely slow fixture builders go behind --full / CI.
Single source of truth for the gate: lattice validate and the REVIEW->TEST gate both run the root npm test chain, so wiring into that chain covers both with one edit.
drivers: Incident: test:process-fact-contract sat RED on main invisibly because it was not in any validate path.
B-3990:F-001 systemic gap: wrapper-root/gitRoot smokes pass standalone but are invisible to validate.
Speed budget: REVIEW->TEST gate and per-commit validate must stay seconds-fast; storydir suite is ~7s.
Lowest-risk wiring given no validate.ts and no validate.command override exists.

options.name: A: chain fast guards into root npm test, slow suite via --full-reachable script
pros: Both lattice validate and REVIEW->TEST gate run them with one edit (they share the npm test fallback).
Zero config-mechanism change; uses the existing fallback discovery path.
A guard failure naturally fails npm test -> fails validate -> blocks the gate (CHK-002 satisfied by construction).
Trivial to reason about which guards are gated (read the test script).
cons: Root test script line gets longer.
Need a separate explicitly-reachable path (test:all / a full aggregator) for the slow suite + 160-smoke run since no validate.ts interprets --full.

options.name: B: add validate.command(s) array to lattice.config.json listing the battery
pros: Could express optional vs required per-command.
cons: Larger surface change to config semantics for a wiring task; config.commands path is less exercised than the npm test fallback.
REVIEW->TEST gate and validate must both honor it; more moving parts to verify.
Higher risk for a maintenance-mode story whose only job is to RUN existing guards.

options.name: C: introduce a project validate.ts that interprets --full and dispatches batteries
pros: Native --full handling (verifier.ts passes --full through to validate.ts).
cons: Largest new surface (a whole new project entrypoint) for a pure wiring story; over-engineering / gold-plating.
Changes the validate execution model (validate.ts takes precedence over npm test), risking unrelated behavior shifts.
Out of proportion to the strict scope.

chosen: A: chain fast guards into root npm test, slow suite via --full-reachable script
rationale: Option A is the minimal, lowest-risk wiring: lattice validate and the REVIEW->TEST gate both fall back to the root npm test chain (confirmed: no validate.ts, no validate.command), so chaining the orphaned fast guards (process-fact-contract, runtime-fact-contract, a new root test:evidence-quality alias, anti-stall) and the fast wrapper-root smokes (storydir-inside-gitroot-smoke, gitroot-cwd-routing, bare-gate-gitroot-cwd, done-oracle-wrapper-root) into root test makes a guard failure block validate by construction (satisfying CHK-002). The slow storydir-inside-gitroot-suite (~7s) and the full 160-smoke test:all stay reachable via a documented full/CI aggregator, not the fast gate. B adds config-semantics risk and C introduces a whole new entrypoint — both disproportionate to a maintenance-mode wiring story (YAGNI). gitroot-cwd-contract is already chained and is excluded to avoid double-running.

preMortem.scenario: A newly-wired guard is actually RED when added, and the implementer excludes it to make the gate pass.
preMortem.trigger: npm test fails on the new guard step.
preMortem.consequence: The story ships a gate that silently omits a real invariant — re-creating the exact regression-blindness this story exists to kill.
preMortem.mitigation: Hard rule baked into PLAN: never exclude a guard to pass. Baseline verified all 9 candidates GREEN on main before wiring; if any goes RED, fix root cause or escalate, do not drop it from the chain.

preMortem.scenario: A guard is added to the root test chain but is ALSO already present (double-run), or added in a way that the REVIEW->TEST gate skips it.
preMortem.trigger: Duplicate npm run line, or guard placed somewhere validate fallback does not execute.
preMortem.consequence: Wasted runtime, or false sense of coverage where the gate does not actually run the guard.
preMortem.mitigation: Audit the existing chain (gitroot-cwd-contract already present -> excluded). Verify in TEST that lattice validate output literally lists each newly-gated guard, and confirm the REVIEW->TEST gate path (same npm test fallback) executes them.

preMortem.scenario: The slow storydir suite (or all 160 smokes) gets accidentally pulled into the fast gate, blowing the speed budget.
preMortem.trigger: Implementer chains test:all or the suite into root test instead of a --full/CI-only path.
preMortem.consequence: Every commit/REVIEW->TEST gate becomes slow, eroding trust in the gate.
preMortem.mitigation: Explicit fast-vs-full split in plan.md: fast guards in root test; storydir-suite + test:all only in a separate full aggregator. TEST step measures the fast-gate delta and confirms it stays seconds-fast.

preMortem.scenario: A guard fails ONLY under the npm test chain (not standalone) due to cwd / env / ordering differences when run via the chain.
preMortem.trigger: A guard relies on cwd or an env var that differs when invoked as npm run inside the root test chain vs run directly.
preMortem.consequence: Spurious RED or, worse, spurious GREEN (guard no-ops in the chained context), defeating the purpose.
preMortem.mitigation: TEST step runs the FULL lattice validate (the real chain), not just standalone guards, and confirms each guard both runs and asserts. CHK-002 breaks a guard and confirms validate actually turns RED on it within the chain.
